data.description: modem.v3's seven states as packed records (core section 7.6; #991), since revision 3.3, beside the JSON states that keep their text. Each ends with an extension marker, so a later minor appends optional fields.

DestinationRecord.description: state `packed/destination/{destination}`: the radio's metrics toward one DLEP destination (DestinationState, documents.rs; RFC 8175 section 13), at the ranges of `Readings`' `link_*`. Its addresses are text, and stay in the JSON destination

EndpointRecord.description: state `packed/sdu/endpoint/{endpoint}`: how many lanes reach the remote, and how many have Zenoh attached (EndpointState, documents.rs); each lane's name is `@op/sdu/lanes`'s

IdentityRecord.description: state `packed/identity`: the equipment identifier, an IMEI's 15 digits (3GPP TS 23.003). The RFC 8348 names and revisions are text, and stay in the JSON `identity`

LinkRecord.description: state `packed/sdu/link`: the medium's capabilities (Capabilities, documents.rs), flattened, and how many lanes it carries and how many have Zenoh attached. Each lane's own facts are `@op/sdu/lanes`'s

OperRecord.description: state `packed/oper`: `oper`'s status, admin state, whether it recovers, its last change, uptime and clock (Oper, modem-contract documents.rs). Its `reason` (the device's words) and `boot_id` stay in the JSON `oper`: the record's run tells driver starts apart

RadioRecord.description: state `packed/radio`: registration and access technology, ModemManager's names with `-` as `_` and 5gnr as nr5g (modem-device's Registration, AccessTechnology)

SecurityRecord.description: state `packed/security`: who provides link security, its scope, and each guarantee as a bit, never one boolean (I6). The principal's name and the note are text, and stay in the JSON `security`; `principal_named` says whether it names one

data.description: modem.v3's readings in one packed record (core section 7.6, 7.7; telemetry.v2; #991), the frame type of frames/fast, frames/slow and frames/paid since revision 3.3. Every field is optional: a device writes a reading it does not have absent, never 0. Each range, resolution and reserved code is zenoh-modem's own bound where its code has one, else a physical one (examples/zk2/zenoh-modem/README.md, "Frames"). A counter's width holds its worst rate between two frames of the slowest cadence (900 s): counts 20 bits, bytes and milliseconds 24, the kernel's packets 32 and its octets 40.

Readings.description: the 73 readings, in the contract's order, each the field of its stream's name with / as _

data.$comment: zenoh-modem modem.v3 (#623). Field names and types follow modem-contract/src/documents.rs and registry/types.toml (v2.14); ParamValue follows zenkey 0.11's zenkey::config. Open content model, as v1's served schemas (zenoh-modem architecture.md §4.6). At port time schemars generates this file from the Rust types and the generated file is committed (contract-crate.md).

ActionEvent.description: stream `action_event/{occurrence}`: an operator action ran, or was refused. Attribution is caller-claimed (O7 call metadata), never authentication (I5).

actor.description: The caller's claimed actor (v1 `?actor=`, zk2 O7 attachment).

ActionOutcome.description: op `action/{name}` reply: what it did and what it cost.

detail.description: One line in the device's words.

ActionRequest.description: op `action/{name}` request: the action's arguments, by name.

Capabilities.description: What the medium behind a device can carry.

framing.description: Explicitly null for a module that sends an SDU as one frame: always present, so 'does not frame' differs from 'did not say'.

listen_before_talk.description: Whether the radio runs channel activity detection before every transmission (#165).

max_batch_size.description: The largest `batch_size` Zenoh may be configured with (tx_max_sdu + the 2-byte length prefix).

reliable.description: Whether the medium delivers in order and without loss.

rx_max_sdu.description: Largest SDU the medium will deliver, in bytes.

sdu_time_ms.description: Milliseconds one full-size SDU costs the medium at the rate it can sustain, a duty budget included (#151); explicitly null where it cannot say.

tx_max_sdu.description: Largest SDU the medium will transmit, in bytes.

Counter.description: A monotonic count, published as a bare JSON number (v1 `Counter`, Rust u64). A decrease is a reset, legitimate only across a continuity epoch (r3.2 §3.5). Values above 2^53 lose precision in readers that parse JSON numbers as doubles.

DestinationState.description: state `destination/{destination}`: one neighbour a netdev's radio reports (#137); deleted when the radio reports it gone. Units are in the field names.

destination.description: The radio's name for it as the key chunk spells it (DLEP: the MAC, lowercase hex with hyphens).

DeviceFault.description: stream `device_fault/{occurrence}`: the medium's own words, verbatim.

lane.description: The lane it concerns; explicitly null when device-wide.

occurrences.description: Transitions this event stands for, itself included.

Duplex.description: Whether the medium can transmit and receive at once.

Empty.description: The request of an operation that takes nothing (v1 read procedures had no body).

EndpointLane.description: One lane, as an endpoint document names it: deliberately reduced (documents.rs:181-195).

EndpointState.description: state `sdu/endpoint/{endpoint}`: one remote, and its lanes.

endpoint.description: The medium's name for this remote (I5: addressing, not identity).

Framing.description: How a module splits an SDU into frames on the air, as it declares it (#159).

Gauge.description: An integer reading that may go down or below zero (v1 `Gauge`, Rust i64).

Identity.description: state `identity`: RFC 8348's fields and the equipment identifier. Never a subscriber identifier (IMSI, ICCID, MSISDN): I5.

imei.description: The bearer's equipment identifier: addressing, never identity (I5).

IdentityChange.description: stream `identity_change/{occurrence}`: the device behind a name changed (#122).

backlog_bytes.description: Bytes Zenoh wrote to this lane's socket that the driver has not read yet (#151); absent where unmeasurable.

connected.description: Whether Zenoh is attached to it right now.

endpoint.description: Which remote it reaches: an addressing identifier, never a proof of identity (I5).

lane.description: The lane's own rendering: endpoint, reliability and rank.

queue_bound_batches.description: Batches the socket holds below Zenoh's scheduler once the driver stops reading (#151); absent where unknown.

rank.description: Scheduling rank; lower is more urgent.

reliable.description: Whether it promises ordered, loss-free delivery.

LaneTable.description: op `sdu/lanes`: the same facts as LinkState, on demand.

LinkState.description: state `sdu/link`: what one device's medium is and what it carries.

device.description: The local device (the service name, repeated as a structured field).

ttl_s.description: Seconds this document stays fresh; refreshed at half this.

Measure.description: A real in the resource's `telemetry.unit` (v1 `Measure`, Rust f64): a dBm has a sign and a fraction. The Rust side carries milli-units; the wire carries the unit.

ModemError.description: The `app` error detail of modem.v3's operations, in the core envelope (O3). v1's [[error]] entries: `action-refused` is modem.v3's; `restart-required` and `device-refused` belong to config.v1's set (config.v1-binding.md).

admin.description: `up` | `down`: radio silence is `down` here, distinct from a failure.

clock_synced.description: Whether the wall clock here is believed synchronised.

last_change_ms.description: Epoch ms of the last status change, by the device's clock.

reason.description: Why, in the device's words, when it is not `up`.

recoverable.description: Whether the device expects to come back on its own.

at_ms.description: Epoch ms, as the driver's clock had it.

event_id.description: The occurrence chunk of the key, repeated.

occurrences.description: Transitions folded into this one under the rate floor; 1 when none.

ParamValue.description: One parameter value, untagged: the configuration plane's three kinds (zenkey::config::ParamValue). Duplicated from config.v1's schema: draft 0 cannot reference another interface's types (README gap 18).

RadioState.description: state `radio`: where a bearer stands with its network (#123).

SecurityState.description: state `security`: properties, never a boolean (I6). There is no `encrypted` field.

authenticated_principal.description: The principal the far side authenticated as; explicitly null, never absent.

guarantees.description: The properties it guarantees, named individually.

provider.description: Who provides link security, if anyone (`none`).

data.description: modem.v3's frame records (core section 7.6, 7.7; telemetry.v2, #983 T4). Every field is optional: a device that cannot answer writes it absent, never 0. The ranges and widths are illustrative. Since revision 3.3 the frames of these types are deprecated, and modem-readings.json carries the readings at zenoh-modem's ranges (#991). A group frame's counters are 32 bits, the kernel's octet counters 40; frames/message's are 24.

Air.description: frames/air: what the module frames and the medium spends: frames, listen-before-talk, airtime, ARQ, slot waste, receive errors, the duty cycle

Bearer.description: frames/bearer: what a bearer reports of its link (DLEP RFC 8175 section 13): rates, latency, resources, quality

If.description: frames/if: the kernel's interface counters and its queue disciplines

Layer.description: frames/layer: what each configured layer refuses and does: aead, address, fec, fragment, compress

LinkReadings.description: frames/link: sdu/dropped_total, sched/queue_depth, air/duty_cycle_available and air/duty_cycle_wait_ms, as core section 7.7's fixtures' Link (63 bits)

Message.description: frames/message: all 73 readings, in the contract's order, every counter at 24 bits (a declared loss: each wraps at 2^24)

Radio.description: frames/radio: what the radio measures: bars, RSSI, RSRP, RSRQ, SNR, error rate

Sched.description: frames/sched: the scheduler's counters, its queue and the lane backlog

Sdu.description: frames/sdu: the SDU plane's nine counters
